title: Real-Time Card & UPI Fraud Detection

blueprintSignals.name: Card velocity 1m/1h/24h
blueprintSignals.definition: count and sum of authorisations in sliding windows keyed by card token
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Windows must close strictly before decision time

blueprintSignals.name: Device-card fan-out
blueprintSignals.definition: distinct cards seen on the device fingerprint in 24h
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Fingerprint must be hashed at event time, not retro-joined

blueprintSignals.name: Merchant risk drift
blueprintSignals.definition: 7-day chargeback rate of the merchant versus its 90-day baseline
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Chargebacks mature in 30-90 days so use matured labels only

blueprintSignals.name: New device for card
blueprintSignals.definition: first time this card token is seen on this device fingerprint
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: The first-seen table must be built from events before the decision, not from full history

blueprintSignals.name: Amount versus card baseline
blueprintSignals.definition: amount divided by the card's trailing 90-day median ticket
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: The baseline must exclude the scored transaction and any fraud already known

blueprintSignals.name: Mule-ring risk scalar
blueprintSignals.definition: component risk and hop distance to known mule seeds, written to the online store every few seconds by a streaming graph worker (Flink with Neo4j or TigerGraph, or incremental connected components)
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Seed list and graph snapshot must be frozen at decision time

blueprintSignals.name: Payload-only score inputs
blueprintSignals.definition: amount, payee MCC, device fingerprint and a local Bloom-filter blocklist hit, all present in the request
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Must read nothing from the store or the fallback silently depends on it

label: For "Real-Time Card & UPI Fraud Detection": Block fraudulent authorisations inside the payment auth path while keeping false declines under 0.3% of genuine volume. Define the label exactly as in milestone M1: what counts as a positive or a correct outcome, and when it becomes known. Design around this trap first: Training on confirmed fraud only hides review-queue selection bias.
